name: Sapphire FUE

lead: Sapphire FUE is a hair transplant in which the recipient channels are cut with sapphire blades rather than steel. Clinics describe finer incisions, about 0.5 to 1.0 mm, that may allow denser placement, less bleeding, faster healing and less visible scarring for a denser hairline.

Follicles are extracted as in standard FUE, then implanted into the channels. Evidence comparing blade types is limited: a 2026 paper compared sapphire and steel blades, and a registered trial studied a topical agent for wound healing after sapphire FUE.

paras: It follows the standard FUE routine under local anaesthetic, with sapphire-tipped blades used to make the recipient sites before grafts are placed. Hair grows in over the following months.
Risks are those of FUE in general, such as swelling, shock loss and folliculitis.

angle.text: Sapphire FUE is promoted as giving hair transplants finer incisions, denser graft placement and faster healing, for a fuller hairline with less visible scarring. The restored hair is visible once it grows in, while comparisons of blade types are limited.

lead: Sapphire FUE is a follicular unit extraction hair transplant in which the recipient sites, the small openings where grafts are placed, are made with sapphire blades instead of steel.[1] It is used to restore hair density and a natural-looking hairline for people with pattern baldness, with clinics promoting finer incisions that allow denser placement and quicker healing.[1][2]

In FUE generally, individual follicular units of one to four hairs are removed under local anaesthesia and the surgeon makes small recipient openings, set in a deliberate density and angle so the result looks natural; FUE leaves small dot-like scars rather than the linear scar of strip harvesting.[2] Grokipedia, an AI-generated source, says sapphire blades are sharper and finer, with possible advantages in bleeding, healing and scar visibility; these are descriptions rather than independently verified findings.[1]
A 2026 prospective observational study of 1000 patients compared sapphire and steel blades and reported higher graft survival with sapphire.[3]

paras: FUE removes individual follicular units with tiny circular punches about 0.6 to 1.0 mm wide and places them in recipient sites made with micro blades or needles.[2] Sapphire FUE changes the blade material of that recipient step.[1] Wikipedia's hair transplantation article does not address blade material; it records common cosmetic goals including male pattern baldness, hairline lowering or reconstruction, eyebrow restoration and scar filling.[2]

Grokipedia describes sapphire blades as allowing denser placement, less bleeding, faster healing and less visible scarring, and gives channel sizes of 0.5 to 1.0 mm.[1] Wikipedia lists shock loss of transplanted hair, a steep learning curve, higher cost and longer surgery time as general characteristics of FUE.[2]

A 2026 prospective observational study in the Journal of Maxillofacial and Oral Surgery followed 1000 hair-restoration patients from January 2024 to March 2025. The sapphire group had higher graft survival (94.7%) than the steel group (88.9%), double-forceps implantation shortened implantation time by 1.3 hours, two-day full-head operations gave higher density (43.2 grafts per cm2) and satisfaction, and half-head sessions healed in 4.6 days versus 6.1.[3] A completed registered trial of 70 participants studied topical rifamycin SV for wound healing after sapphire FUE.[4] The 2026 study was observational rather than randomized.

timeline.event: Registered trial of topical rifamycin SV after sapphire FUE begins.[4]
Observational comparison of sapphire and steel FUE blades published.[3]
